judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's exemplar is exact and I confirmed the mechanism. worksheet.pdf problem 3 prints three lettered slots: (a) 'How many committees of 3 can be formed altogether?', (b) 'How many of them consist entirely of seniors?', (c) the exact probability. answer_key.pdf's Quick Answers row reads '3. 4, 84, 1/21' — 4 first, 84 second — while the worked solution on the same page correctly gives 'Step 1 (part a) ... = 84' and 'Step 2 (part b) ... = 4'. The cause is visible in verify.json: id 3's entries are listed in the order {n=4,k=3}->4, then {n=9,k=3}->84, then the probability, and scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry() joins expected values in raw JSON array order with no sub-part labels. So the bank is not a transcription slip, it is the array order printed verbatim. The judge also called two manual items reviewed and the rest of the mathematics correct; I re-derived all twelve independently and agree — C(7,3)=35, (x+2)^3, C(9,3)=84 / C(4,3)=4 / 1/21, Pascal 84+126=210, (2x-1)^4 = 16x^4-32x^3+24x^2-8x+1, C(6,4)=15 and 15/64, C(8,5)*3^3 = 56*27 = 1512, 10*7/220 = 7/22, C(5,3)(0.7)^3(0.3)^2 = 3087/10000, C(6,3)*2^3 = 160, C(5,2)=10 and 5/16, C(8,2)=28 and 28*(1/16)(729/4096) = 5103/16384. Two things the judge missed, both aggravating rather than contradicting: (1) problem 8's bank row prints '10, 7, 220, 7/22' — four values for three printed slots, and part (a)'s actual answer, 10*7 = 70, never appears anywhere in the bank even though the key's Step 1 gives it; (2) problem 4 asks the student to 'state the relationship between the three values and explain where it appears in Pascal's triangle', an explanation slot, yet verify.json id 4 carries three eval entries and no manual entry, and final_response.md defends this explicitly ('Problem 4's state-the-relationship is answered in full in the key; its three numeric values are machine-verified'), which is precisely the open-response-not-flagged pattern the prompt asked to avoid.

strengths_to_preserve: The interleaving is genuinely method-forcing rather than cosmetic: problem 8 (3 marbles from 5 red and 7 blue, drawn all at once) sits two items away from problem 9 (5 independent free throws at p = 0.7), and the key's problem 8 Step 3 names the distinction out loud — 'because the marbles are drawn without replacement, the coefficients multiply on top and divide by a single coefficient below — this is not the C(n,k) p^k q^(n-k) formula, which needs independent trials'. The study guide mirrors this by placing its counting section (3) immediately before its binomial section (4) and stating the reason for the adjacency.

Problem 7 is a designed trap with the trap named in the solution: 'Answering 56 is the standard slip: the binomial coefficient counts the terms, but the constant raised to its power belongs to the coefficient too.' The verify entry backs the full answer rather than the coefficient alone — expr 'factorial(n)/(factorial(k)*factorial(n-k)) * 3**(n-k)' at n=8,k=5 expecting 1512 — so the trap value cannot drift from the checked value.

Problem 11's manual-review note is a usable rubric, not a gesture: 'accept any sentence saying that Jo used the ratio of heads to flips instead of the ratio of favourable outcomes to total outcomes, or that the arrangement count C(5,2) was omitted', and the distractor 2/5 is contrasted numerically against 5/16 = 0.3125 in the worked solution.

The synthesis item (12) closes the loop the sheet opened: it makes the student write the (q+p)^8 term whose coefficient IS the count of which components are defective, and the key's Step 3 ties expansion to counting and then observes that q + p = 1 makes the nine terms a complete distribution — the conceptual payoff for 'one set of numbers, two jobs'.
final_response.md's page counts are measured, not narrated: it claims worksheet 7 / key 4 / study guide 2 and pdfinfo reports exactly 7, 4 and 2.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py builds each bank row by joining a problem's expected values in verify.json array order with no sub-part labels and no binding to the worksheet's printed (a)/(b)/(c) markers. When the author lists a problem's checks in solution-discovery order rather than in printed order, the bank prints the right values against the wrong parts, and no gate can notice because every individual value is verified. Problem 3 is the reversal; problem 8 is the same defect in its other form, where an intermediate check (10, then 7) is banked and the composed answer the slot asks for (70) is not banked at all.
evidence: verify.json id 3 entry order: {'at': {'n': 4, 'k': 3}, 'expected': 4} precedes {'at': {'n': 9, 'k': 3}, 'expected': 84}; worksheet.pdf problem 3 prints (a) total committees then (b) all-senior committees.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '3. 4, 84, 1/21' while the same page's worked solution prints 'Step 1 (part a) ... 84' and 'Step 2 (part b) ... 4'.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '8. 10, 7, 220, 7/22' for a three-slot problem; the key's Step 1 gives part (a) as 10 * 7 = 70, a value absent from the bank.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry(): 'vals = [e["expected"] for e in entries ...]' then '", ".join(_fmt(v) for v in vals)' — order is the JSON array, labels are never emitted.

root_causes.description: An item that asks for an explanation was recorded as fully machine-verified. Problem 4's third request ('state the relationship between the three values and explain where it appears in Pascal's triangle') has no manual entry in verify.json; its three eval entries cover only 84, 126 and 210. The final response then reports 'two items flagged for manual review' when three worksheet items contain open writing, so a teacher using the flag list to plan grading time will not know to read problem 4's explanation.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 4: 'then state the relationship between the three values and explain where it appears in Pascal's triangle.'
verify.json id 4: three entries, all type 'eval' (expected 84, 126, 210); no entry of type 'manual'.
final_response.md: 'Flagged for manual review — two items ... Problem 4's state-the-relationship is answered in full in the key; its three numeric values are machine-verified.'
answer_key.pdf problem 4 prints a full prose justification with no 'Manual review' note, unlike problems 11 and 12 which both carry one.

improvements.title: Bind each Quick Answers value to its printed sub-part instead of printing verify.json array order
improvements.proposed_change: Add a required 'slot' field to every verify entry belonging to a multi-entry problem id — either the printed sub-part letter ('a', 'b', 'c') or a short caption ('total committees'). scripts/render_quick_answers.py must sort a row by slot and print 'a) 84; b) 4; c) 1/21' rather than a bare comma list in array order, and must fall back to the worksheet's own (a)/(b)/(c) markers, never to array position, when slots are absent. Reject at gate time any problem whose number of banked values differs from its number of printed response slots, which also catches problem 8's four-values-for-three-slots row and forces the author to bank the composed answer 70 rather than the intermediates 10 and 7.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture using curr-440's own verify.json id 3 (entries ordered 4, 84, 1/21) plus a worksheet stem whose sub-parts are ordered total-then-seniors. Assert the rendered bank row is 'a) 84; b) 4; c) 1/21'. Today's renderer produces '4, 84, 1/21' so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after. A second case feeds id 8 (10, 7, 220, 7/22) against a three-slot stem and asserts a non-zero exit naming the slot-count mismatch.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the single hard failure that made this case a REJECT and repairs the second, unreported mismatch on problem 8. Generalises to every multi-part problem in the run, where the current row format silently depends on the order the author happened to write the checks.
improvements.risk: Labelled rows are wider, so the adaptive column_count() heuristic will drop more banks to two columns and lengthen the key by a fraction of a page. Requiring slot fields also invalidates existing verify JSONs until they are migrated, so the gate should warn before it errors.

improvements.title: Flag problem 4's 'explain where it appears in Pascal's triangle' as a manual item rather than counting it machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Make the manual-flag rule mechanical rather than judgemental: any worksheet stem containing an explanation verb ('explain', 'state the relationship', 'describe', 'justify', 'why') must have at least one verify entry of type 'manual' bound to that stem, and the answer key must print the corresponding 'Manual review:' acceptance note. Add the check to the gate that already counts declared vs printed problems, and update SKILL.md so 'the key answers it in full' is explicitly NOT a substitute for a manual flag — the flag exists to tell the grader that a human must read the student's sentence, not to admit the author does not know the answer.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 4 stem contains 'state the relationship ... and explain where it appears in Pascal's triangle' with verify entries of type 'eval' only. The gate must exit non-zero naming problem 4's unflagged explanation slot; adding a manual entry with a desc makes it pass, and the rendered key must then carry a 'Manual review (part c)' line for that problem as problems 11 and 12 already do.
improvements.expected_impact: Corrects the manual-item count reported to the teacher (two -> three here) and stops explanation slots from being counted inside 'every machine-checkable answer was verified'. Directly addresses the prompt clause 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review'.
improvements.risk: Keyword matching will over-trigger on stems that merely say 'show the cancellation' or 'explain your working' as a study habit rather than a graded response, so the rule needs a small allow-list or an author override with a recorded reason, otherwise manual counts inflate and the flag loses meaning.

case_summary: A strong interleaved binomial-coefficient set — twelve problems, correct mathematics throughout (I re-derived all of them), a real method-choice design that puts a without-replacement marble draw next to an independent-trials free-throw problem and names the difference in the key, and a two-page study guide whose four sections each carry a rule, a worked example and a distinct try-it. It is rejected for one printed defect and, on my reading, for a second the judge did not report. The Quick Answers bank prints problem 3 as '4, 84, 1/21' against a worksheet that asks for the total first and the all-senior count second, because scripts/render_quick_answers.py joins expected values in verify.json array order without sub-part labels; problem 8 fails the same way, banking the intermediates 10 and 7 and never printing part (a)'s actual answer, 70. Separately, problem 4's 'explain where it appears in Pascal's triangle' is an open response with no manual entry, and final_response.md defends that choice, so the teacher is told two items need reading when three do. Nothing here is a mathematical error; both defects live in the layer between verified values and the printed teacher-facing artifact.
